chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: Casino Simpson and the Chicago pianists before Earl Hines
summary: Chicago was big after Caldwell left; Casino Simpson, a Wilberforce classmate, imitated Fats Waller and Earl Hines.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yes, I get you. Well, of course, we -- you sort of -- in a way, you left Chicago before -- I mean the biggest days, didn't you?
Certainly, yes, sir, he did.
You know, I mean after you'd gone, went on I mean there was a lot (unintelligible) done there.
That's right.
And Earl Hines came.
Yeah, Earl Hines came there. Quite a few of the fellows came there.
Well, what -- there was one thing I was going to ask you was -- we skipped over that, but Casino Simpson was in that --
Casino Simpson.
Well, how did he play in those days?
He was a fine pianist (unintelligible) -- we all came up together in school, Casino, Self, Homer, Cecil Irwin (unintelligible) --
Oh, Casino came out of Wilberforce?
Yeah.
Well, tell me something. One of -- now, I forget who it was -- said that -- oh, I know who it was. It was Franz Jackson.
Franz Jackson?
Yeah, he told me he played in the band -- Casino's band.
Yeah.
And he said, yes, he was a great piano player.
He was.
But, he said, he played like everybody. He said, now I'm going to play like Fats Waller.
(Laughter)
And he could. And he said, now I'm going to play like Earl Hines. So I never could quite figure -- I mean when I've heard Casino, he sounds as though he was doing an imitation of Earl.
Well, he would. He could imitate most any of the piano -- that's before Earl Hines came to Chicago. Like they had different ones around there playing piano.
